messages:
nate: FYI — customer ACME (ticket 4921) reports tool/function call failures. Their payloads are being cut mid-stream, causing schema validation errors like 'unexpected end of JSON input'. Happening intermittently.
acme-integration: seeing ~3% of calls fail. We get a 400 from Redwood: \"invalid_tool_args: JSON parse error\". Sample body attached to ticket.
support-bot: Created escalation to eng-runtime and added logs from the customer.
michael: can you paste the exact truncated snippet and the request-id header from one failing call?
acme-integration: snippet (copied from their capture): ```{"action":"charge_card","amount":1200,"currency":"USD","metadata":{"order_id":"ORD-993"}  ``` — note missing closing braces at end. request-id: req_0f9c3b
olivia: thanks. any common pattern? chunk sizes, proxies in front?
acme-integration: they route through Cloudflare Spectrum -> internal LB -> our hosted endpoint. Failures spike when payloads > 6KB or when args contain emojis. They mentioned keepalive heartbeats on client side.
michael: quick hypothesis: chunk boundary clipping causing multibyte UTF-8 sequences to be split and our streamer tries to interpret partial runes, producing a shorter byte sequence and final event missing trailing braces. Need to see raw transfer encoding.
janet: tagging eng-runtime oncall — can you reproduce locally with a client that sends chunked Transfer-Encoding streaming where a JSON field crosses a chunk boundary?
eng-runtime-bot: oncall pinged: eng-runtime assigned to #oncall
nate: repro steps request: please provide a minimal curl or node script simulating chunked upload and keepalive newline insertion.
acme-integration: here's a simple Node repro they ran:
```js
const http = require('http');
const req = http.request({method:'POST', path:'/v1/stream', headers:{'Transfer-Encoding':'chunked'}}, res=>{});
req.write('{"action":"charge_card","args":{"note":"');
setTimeout(()=> req.write('\uD83D'), 10); // high surrogate only
setTimeout(()=> req.write('\uDE0A","amount":1200}}'), 20);
req.end();
```
support-bot: customer reports that when the surrogate halves split across chunks some servers/transport layers drop or re-chunk and the final event arrives truncated.
michael: repro successful locally — when a multibyte emoji pair is split across two chunks some intermediate proxies re-chunk and end up delivering an incomplete sequence before we finish assembling event frames, leading to the JSON ending early.
olivia: can you show the server-side log where our parser errors with the request-id?
michael: log: `2026-03-10T12:08:45Z req=req_0f9c3b parse_error: invalid_tool_args: unexpected end of JSON input at position 128`
janet: does our streaming parser validate UTF-8 continuity before attempting JSON.parse on the assembled slice?
michael: currently we attempt incremental JSON tokenization on incoming event bytes; we assume chunks preserve UTF-8 boundaries — bad assumption. We'll change to accumulate bytes and validate Utf8 (using utf8::is_valid) before handing to JSON tokenizer.
nate: mitigation for customer: ask them to switch to sending with Content-Length (non-chunked) for critical toolcalls, or ensure emoji sequences are not split, as short-term workaround.
acme-integration: can you provide a quick toggle we can set on our side? We'll try Content-Length. Also please confirm ETA for fix.
michael: I'll open a PR with fix (accumulate+utf8-check and stricter framing) and a unit test for split runes. Targeting patch release tomorrow EOD UTC.
olivia: thanks. once PR lands, can we get a canary build for ACME to test before full rollout?
michael: yes — will coordinate with eng-release. I'll attach a canary image and instructions.
janet: noted — updating ticket 4921 with repro, logs, workaround, and planned fix ETA. setting customer expectation.
acme-integration: appreciate the quick turnaround. we'll test Content-Length and report back.
nate: closing loop for now — if customer still sees >0.1% failures after the workaround, re-open and we'll escalate to full incident. :thumbsup:
